description: Tick-normalized height-mode time-lock vectors: nLockTime, nSequence, and coinbase maturity. T(x) is the cumulative tick of block x, inclusive of its own interval, from the schedule. Height-mode predicates: nLockTime is strict and absolute — final in block b iff T(b) > 600*lockTime; nSequence is weak and relative — mature in block b iff T(b) - T(fundingBlock) >= 600*relativeLock; coinbase maturity is weak and absolute — spendable in block b iff T(b) - T(creationBlock) >= 60,000. Mempool forms use T(tip+1) from the schedule, never T(tip)+tau(tip). BCHN escape clauses: nLockTime==0 is final everywhere; every-input-SEQUENCE_FINAL is final regardless of nLockTime. A coinbase transaction is exempt from both predicates, but only from H_a + 1 onward: at or before H_a both fields bind and the coinbase is evaluated like any other transaction. The exemption is a scope restriction on the predicates, so it lives in the caller behind the same upgrade predicate the rest of the rule set uses; the coinbase vectors model that short circuit via `subjectIsCoinbase`, gated on the upgrade boundary at H_a + 1, and lock_noncoinbase_bip54_twin pins that an identical non-coinbase is still bound. Coinbase maturity is unaffected, because it reads the spent output's height and a coinbase spends none. MTP-mode comparison and the LOCKTIME_THRESHOLD split are unchanged and out of scope. Every expected value is a hand-derived golden pin; the generator verifies the shared reference evaluators (timelock_ticks.h) against the pins and refuses to emit on any mismatch. All integer values are decimal strings to preserve full 64-bit precision.

vectors.name: lock_escape_zero
vectors.note: nLockTime==0 is final at every block via the BCHN escape, even with a non-final input sequence

vectors.name: lock_escape_all_seqfinal
vectors.note: absolute nLockTime is a no-op when every input is SEQUENCE_FINAL; the CHIP example release at 1,000,111 only holds with a non-final sequence

vectors.name: lock_pre_L1
vectors.note: strict: T(b) > 600 means T(1)=600 is still non-final

vectors.name: lock_pre_L100
vectors.note: legacy release block = L+1

vectors.name: seq_pre_n1_c100
vectors.note: weak: equality at c+n satisfies

vectors.name: seq_pre_n6_c100
vectors.note: legacy release block = c+n

vectors.name: mat_pre_c0
vectors.note: genesis coinbase: 60,000 ticks = 100 blocks

vectors.name: mat_pre_c500000
vectors.note: legacy release block = c+100

vectors.name: lock_post_doc
vectors.note: CHIP example: nLocktime=1,000,011 releases at block 1,000,111, the first block whose tick exceeds 600*1,000,011 = 600,006,600

vectors.name: lock_post_600grid
vectors.note: strictness where 600*L (600,006,000) is exactly a block tick (block 1,000,100)

vectors.name: lock_post_Ha
vectors.note: lock naming the activation height releases at the first 1-minute block; L <= H_a keeps release = L+1

vectors.name: lock_post_pre_Ha
vectors.note: pre-activation lock: release = L+1 exactly as legacy, because blocks <= H_a are 600-tick

vectors.name: seq_post_fund_Ha_n1
vectors.note: one normalized unit (600 ticks) = ten 1-minute blocks; mempool MUST use T(tip+1) from the schedule, not T(tip)+tau(tip)

vectors.name: seq_post_n1_c1000010
vectors.note: post-activation funding: +10 blocks per normalized unit

vectors.name: seq_post_straddle
vectors.note: funded 10 blocks before activation with n=10 releases exactly at activation

vectors.name: seq_multi_300tick
vectors.note: in a 300-tick segment one normalized unit = 2 blocks

vectors.name: mat_post_fund_Ha
vectors.note: coinbase created in the last 600-tick block matures after exactly 1,000 one-minute blocks

vectors.name: mat_post_c1001000
vectors.note: post-activation coinbase: 60,000 ticks = 1,000 blocks

vectors.name: mat_post_straddle
vectors.note: coinbase 100 blocks before activation (60,000 ticks) matures exactly at activation

vectors.name: mat_multi_300tick
vectors.note: 60,000 ticks = 200 blocks in a 300-tick segment

vectors.name: lock_multi_300tick
vectors.note: strictness where 600*L (30,060,000) is exactly a block tick inside a 300-tick segment

vectors.name: lock_coinbase_bip54_h_plus_2
vectors.note: BIP-54 template stamping nLockTime = height - 1 with a non-final input sequence, as it lands in block H_a + 2 (1,000,002) where the value is 1,000,001. Below H_a + 1 the pre-activation rule governs and block H_a rejects the stamp; from H_a + 1 the exemption makes it final in every block, which is what keeps that template valid. The check at 1,000,010 is the endpoint of that range and the sharp one: T(1,000,010) = 600,000,600 equals the boundary 600 * 1,000,001 exactly, so the strict > is what would reject it, while lock_noncoinbase_bip54_twin pins the identical fields as false there. Without the exemption the raw predicate would call 1,000,002..1,000,010 non-final -- T(1,000,002) = 600,000,120 is far short -- recovering only at 1,000,011.

vectors.name: lock_coinbase_bip54_h_plus_1
vectors.note: The other half of the BIP-54 pair: block H_a + 1 carries nLockTime = 1,000,000. Below the gate the field binds -- at block H_a itself 1,000,000 is not below 1,000,000 and the input sequence is non-final, so the pre-activation rule rejects it -- while the exemption makes it final at H_a + 1, where the raw tick predicate 600,000,060 > 600,000,000 would also have cleared it. Pinned so the handover is visible: the same fields are non-final exactly one block earlier.

vectors.name: lock_coinbase_time_mode
vectors.note: Time-mode nLockTime (>= LOCKTIME_THRESHOLD), far ahead of any block timestamp: the harness supplies nBlockTime = 0, so the pre-activation time-mode arm reports non-final everywhere at or below H_a. The exemption covers the time-mode arm too, but only from H_a + 1.

vectors.name: lock_coinbase_zero_sequence
vectors.note: nSequence 0x00000000 with a height-mode locktime naming 1,000,011: the raw tick predicate, without the exemption, would only clear it at 1,000,111. 'Whatever the nSequence' is the arm pinned here -- the exemption does not read it, and it starts at H_a + 1 like every other upgraded rule.

vectors.name: lock_noncoinbase_bip54_twin
vectors.note: Non-coinbase twin of lock_coinbase_bip54_h_plus_2: identical fields, only the subject differs, and the raw predicate binds unchanged. This is what makes the exemption a restriction on scope rather than a relaxation of the two predicates for everyone.

vectors.name: lock_coinbase_pre_activation_binds
vectors.note: The exemption is a post-upgrade rule, not an unconditional property of coinbases: with nLockTime = 1 and a non-final sequence this coinbase is non-final at blocks 0 and 1 and final from block 2, all well below H_a. A harness that bypassed every coinbase would report release 0 here -- which is exactly the defect this family shipped with.
